title: Why the blues sound best in E-flat and B-flat
summary: Phillips explains that blues are best in E-flat and B-flat, less in C, and declines to name a blues player he dislikes.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: Did you guys used to play Blues in all keys, or just a few favorite keys? What keys mostly did you play Blues in?
In E-flat and B-flat. That's a Blues key. Blues don't sound good in them other keys.
Well, they sound pretty good in D-flat.

But Blues don't sound good in C. They're all right. It's like you take "C-Jam Blues," it's all right. But you can't get the feeling out of that key that you can in B-flat and E-flat. E-Flat is the best key for Blues. I mean, to get that good Blues feeling, way down there. That's when you find a whole lot of these guitar players out here that play the Blues, these guitars that string along, they're just playing, they don't know what chords or nothing. They play the Blues and they don't know... I shouldn't say this, but...
You were talking about this jam session. Did you have something else you were going to say about that?
I had something I was going to say about
the Blues, but it's very personal. I can't say that to them.

Somebody who plays the Blues that I don't like. I don't want to say that. Call no names, you know. Because this thing is liable to be published or somebody will read it, and they'll be mad at me. They'll want to know why the hell I'm saying that about them.
